pending_commit.commit_message: CHROMIUM: [media] rockchip-vpu: Make sure default formats are available Currently there are global macros used to define default formats. This is incorrect because certain hardware variants do not support formats currently defined as default, which leads to initial driver state being incorrect (e.g. pointers which are expected to be valid end up being NULL). Fix this by removing global macros and instead choosing the first available format for given hardware variant. CHROMIUM: [media] rockchip-vpu: Reset raw format when coded format changes Support for raw format and resolution depends on selected coded format, so whenever S_FMT is called on the queue that works on coded data, we need to make sure that raw video queue has a valid format. Current code does not do so. To fix the problem, let's reset raw format to default whenever coded format changes just to stay on the safe side and keep driver state sane. The exact format does not matter at this point, since the API mandates the user to always set the raw format after coded format. BUG=chrome-os-partner:62115 TEST=Run VDA unittest on Kevin Change-Id: I2f3bcc20a814b975d50c3cb41476061ecf88e85b Signed-off-by: Tomasz Figa <tfiga@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/435062 Reviewed-by: Pawel Osciak <posciak@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: drm/rockchip: psr: Avoid redundant calls to .set() callback The first time after we call rockchip_drm_do_flush() after rockchip_drm_psr_register(), we go from PSR_DISABLE to PSR_FLUSH. The difference between PSR_DISABLE and PSR_FLUSH is whether or not we have a delayed work pending - PSR is off in either state. However psr_set_state() only catches the transition from PSR_FLUSH to PSR_DISABLE (which never happens), while going from PSR_DISABLE to PSR_FLUSH triggers a call to psr->set() to disable PSR while it's already disabled. This triggers the eDP PHY power-on sequence without being shut down first and this seems to occasionally leave the encoder unable to later enable PSR. Let's just simplify the state machine and simply consider PSR_DISABLE and PSR_FLUSH the same state. This lets us represent the hardware state by a simple boolean called "enabled" and, while at it, rename the misleading "active" boolean to "inhibit", which represents the purpose much better. Also, userspace can (and does) trigger the rockchip_drm_do_flush() path from drmModeDirtyFB() at any time, whether or the encoder is active. If no mode is set, we call into analogix_dp_psr_set() which returns -EINVAL because encoder->crtc is NULL. Avoid this by starting out with psr->allowed set to false. BUG=chrome-os-partner:57121 TEST=continuously reboot and verify we don't get "Failed to apply PSR -110" Change-Id: I92fe6014080b19669bb17f092298654109058534 Signed-off-by: Kristian H. Kristensen <hoegsberg@chromium.org> Signed-off-by: Tomasz Figa <tfiga@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/436571

CHROMIUM: drm/rockchip: psr: Sanitize semantics of allow/disallow API Currently both rockchip_drm_psr_activate() and _deactivate() only set the boolean "active" flag without actually making sure that hardware state complies with it. Since we are going to extend the usage of this API to properly lock PSR for the duration of atomic commits, we change the semantics in following way: - a counter is used to track the number of disallow requests, - PSR is actually disabled in hardware on first disallow request, - PSR enable work is scheduled on last disallow request. The above allows using the API as a way to deterministically synchronize PSR state changes with other DRM events, i.e. atomic commits and cursor updates. As a nice side effect, the naming is sorted out and we have "inhibit" for stopping the software logic and "enable" for hardware state. BUG=chrome-os-partner:62479 TEST=Pick CL:436410, no more iommu errors upon screen wakeup Change-Id: Ibc9c139806e294e32e9086fc3d4d39c2df4f9ab4 Signed-off-by: Tomasz Figa <tfiga@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/438228 Reviewed-by: Kristian H. CHROMIUM: drm/rockchip: psr: Disallow PSR for the whole atomic commit Instead of leaving the field open for races with the work scheduled and assummed (potentially incorrectly for long modesets) to finish already after the commit, let's just block the PSR completely before hardware programming part begins and unblock after it ends. This relies on reference counted PSR disable introduced with previous patch. factory_restart: gracefully stop goofy factory_restart was sending SIGTERM and SIGKILL to stop factory programs, this would cause Goofy stop immediately, goofy.destory() would not be called, and thus some daemon processes started by goofy (e.g. instalog) would not be stopped. This CL adds an extra step to factory_restart, it will first use SIGINT to stop goofy, and then try SIGTERM and SIGKILL.
